Read observed data defined in a calibration setup table

Source: R/calibrar-main.R
calibration_data.Rd

Build the observed object used by calibration_objFn() from a setup table created with calibration_setup(). Each active row in the setup table points to a file containing observed data, and this function reads those files into a named list whose elements correspond to the calibration variables.

Usage

calibration_data(setup, path = ".", file = NULL, verbose = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

setup

A calibration setup table, usually created with calibration_setup().

path

Base directory used to resolve relative paths from setup$file. Each file is looked up with base::file.path() using path and the value stored in the corresponding file row.

file

Optional path to save the resulting observed object with base::saveRDS(). This is useful when observed data are expensive to read repeatedly.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print progress messages describing which variables were loaded.

...

Additional arguments passed to utils::read.csv() when reading text files.

Value

A named list with one element per row of setup. Element names are taken from setup$variable.

Depending on the corresponding setup row, each element is typically one of:

  • a numeric vector, when varid selects a single column from a text file;

  • a numeric matrix, when a full table is read from a text file;

  • an arbitrary R object read from an .rds file;

  • NA, when use_data = FALSE or calibrate = FALSE.

Details

Rows with use_data = FALSE are kept in the output as NA. This makes it possible to include penalty-only components in the same calibration workflow: such rows still participate in calibration_objFn() provided the model returns a simulated component with the same name.

Only rows satisfying both setup$calibrate and setup$use_data are actually read from disk. All other rows are represented as NA in the returned list.

File reading currently depends on file type:

text files (.csv, .txt)

Read with utils::read.csv(). If varid is supplied, that column is extracted and returned as a numeric vector. Otherwise the full table is converted to a numeric matrix after dropping the first col_skip columns, when applicable.

R objects (.rds)

Read with base::readRDS() and returned as-is.

netCDF (.nc)

Not currently supported by the implementation.

The interpretation of varid, col_skip, and nrows is controlled by the corresponding columns in setup, after defaults have been filled by calibration_setup().

Expected alignment with model outputs

The names of the returned list are used later by calibration_objFn() to match observed and simulated quantities. For each active calibration row, setup$variable must therefore match the name of the corresponding element in the list returned by the model function.

Saving and reusing observed data

When file is supplied, the created list is also saved as an .rds file. This can be helpful in iterative calibration workflows where the setup table is stable but reading the original data files repeatedly is inconvenient.

See also

calibration_setup(), calibration_objFn(), objFn()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
demo = calibrar_demo(model = "PredatorPrey")
setup = calibration_setup(file = demo$setup)
observed = calibration_data(setup = setup, path = demo$path)

names(observed)
str(observed)
} # }
